name: Judas Iscariot
title: The Betrayer
summary: Judas Iscariot was one of Jesus' twelve apostles and the one who betrayed him. He served as the group's treasurer and stole from the money bag. For thirty silver coins, he identified Jesus to the chief priests with a kiss. Afterwards, he regretted his actions, threw the money into the temple, and took his own life.

keyEvents.title: Chosen as an Apostle
keyEvents.description: Judas Iscariot was chosen as one of the twelve apostles. He is always listed last, with the addition 'the one who betrayed him'.

keyEvents.title: The Treasurer Who Stole
keyEvents.description: Judas held the money bag but stole from it. He criticized Mary for anointing Jesus with expensive oil.

keyEvents.title: The Agreement to Betray
keyEvents.description: Judas went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him in exchange for betraying Jesus. They gave him thirty silver coins.

keyEvents.title: The Kiss of Betrayal
keyEvents.description: In Gethsemane, Judas betrayed Jesus with a kiss - the signal he had agreed upon with the soldiers.

keyEvents.title: The remorse and death
keyEvents.description: When Judas saw that Jesus was condemned, he repented, threw the silver coins into the temple, went away and hanged himself.
